author: sonnet
label: c2-seed-sonnet-01
changes: Moved Lag check before Fence A so an over-RPO refusal leaves A serving and unfenced.
Defined the control store and the run record, since the brief requires a place for the active-region record and run state.
Specified fencing as the apps polling the record and failing closed, plus a wait before promote, because fencing must work with A unreachable.
Added what on-call does and what the probes check, matching the brief.
Added promote success check and a timeout, the jobs reset of running rows to queued, health check failure handling, and the DNS TTL effect.
Added resume and abort rules for interrupted runs, plus an open questions section listing the unknown authority, control store product and unmeasured timings.
Take run record: removed the implied automatic resume of a dead run; a second invocation refuses and a person resumes explicitly (answers Q9, avoids a lease).
Added a Failover command note: runs outside A, progress kept in the run record, rerun resumes (Q10).
Added Control store unavailable note and a sentence that A's apps and the command must reach the store (Q11).
Fence A: A's /healthz now fails while A refuses writes, so a store-isolated A pages on-call; added a note on recovery (Q12).
Added What users see note for the window between fence and DNS switch (Q13).
Added an open question for where the failover command runs and a caveat that a store in B alone fails together with B.
Lag check: added that the recorded lag is only a lower bound on loss, and later writes are unknown until A is compared with B (Q14).
Scale up B: added that B's apps and workers follow the same active-region rule and accept writes only when it says B (Q15).
Interrupted or failed runs: abort is now a named --abort flag that sets the record back to A and marks the run aborted (Q16).
Switch DNS: added that the run record is marked done and kept, the active-region record stays B, and returning A keeps refusing writes (Q17).
Fence A: stated that the 30 s wait relies on timing alone and does not check A's /healthz (Q18).
Probes, On-call and A-cut-off notes: A's /healthz failure now carries a reason (fenced or control store unreachable), and on-call reads the active-region record before deciding (Q19).
Reordered to the skill layout: summary, how today's system works, terms, diagram, numbered steps, rules, failure table, open questions.
Added a Terms section defining control store, active-region record, run record, fence, fail closed, idempotent job, failover command, plus RPO/RTO and WAL in line.

Turned the bulleted notes into 10 numbered steps matching the diagram nodes, each with trigger, action and failure handling. The old On-call, Scale up and Health check bullets were split into their own steps.
Merged the scattered failure bullets (interrupted or failed runs, control store unavailable, A cut off from the store) into one failure table; abort rules moved there.
Moved Sessions, Failback and What users see into one short list of rules that apply throughout.
Cut repeated text: the 30 s fence wait reasoning, the run-record resume explanation and the second-run refusal are each said once.
Added the existing-system description (12 and 2 instances, replica lag recording, jobs table, per-region Redis, 60 s TTL) and the RPO/RTO targets from the brief; these were only implied before.
Open questions now also cover who may use the override and the /healthz reason format.
holes: Q2: What does On-call actually do before running the failover command? What do they check or decide, and who has authority to trigger it? (author: On-call confirms A is really lost and decides to run the command; a person always starts it. Who has formal authority to trigger it is not known; added under open questions.)

Q10: Where does the failover command run (whose machine or which service)? What happens if it crashes or loses its network partway through a step? (author: The brief only says a person runs a single command. I decided it must run outside region A (on-call's machine or a jump host). The exact machine or service is not known; added to open questions. If it crashes mid-step, the run record holds the last completed step and rerunning with resume continues, since every step is safe to repeat.)
